dascp.note: Knowledge-soundness is a precondition for any settlement proof to be meaningful: a fraud- or validity-proof scheme used to evidence settlement legs must itself be knowledge-sound.
Auditing ZK-mediated actions presupposes the proofs being audited are knowledge-sound; the audit trail otherwise records assertions of unknown validity.

descriptions.semantic: A prover that convinces the verifier of a statement with non-negligible probability must actually 'know' a valid witness — formalized by an efficient extractor that, given black-box (or rewinding) access to such a prover, outputs a witness satisfying the relation. At the circuit level this is the requirement that the constraint system fully pins down the computation: there are no under-constrained signals an adversary could freely set to forge acceptance of a false statement.
descriptions.system_theoretic: An integrity constraint on the proof system viewed as a relation between (statement, proof) pairs and witnesses: the set of statements for which an accepting proof exists equals (up to negligible error) the language of true statements, AND a witness is efficiently recoverable. The 'no free signal' circuit condition is the concrete, checkable surrogate.
descriptions.security: The integrity backbone of any verifiable-computation system (rollup validity proofs, ZK bridges, private payments). Its failure is acceptance of false statements: minting unbacked assets, validating an invalid state transition, double-spending. Distinct from and independent of ZK/privacy (BPO:0003): a system can be sound but leaky, or hiding but unsound.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Manifests in the arithmetization (R1CS, Plonkish, AIR): every output and intermediate signal must be constrained as a deterministic function of inputs; missing constraints (forgotten boolean/range checks, unconstrained inverses or quotients, under-constrained outputs) leave degrees of freedom. The dominant real-world ZK bug is exactly this under-constraint — not a privacy leak.
descriptions.formal_verification: The cryptographic statement (extractor exists) is proved by reduction, mechanizable in EasyCrypt / proof assistants. The circuit surrogate (full constraint / determinism) is checkable by dedicated static analyzers and SMT: prove that the public inputs uniquely determine all signals, i.e. the constraint system has a unique satisfying completion.

formalization.signature: Relation R ⊆ X×W; argument system (P,V); accept predicate V(x,π)∈{0,1}; circuit C with public inputs xpub, witness signals w, constraints {cᵢ(xpub,w)=0}.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Knowledge soundness:  ∃ PPT extractor E . ∀ P* . Pr[V(x, P*(x))=1] = ε > negl  ⇒  Pr[(x, E^{P*}(x)) ∈ R] ≥ poly(ε) − negl.
Circuit determinism (surrogate):  ∀ xpub . | { w : ∀i. cᵢ(xpub,w)=0 } |  is consistent with exactly the intended computation  (no spurious satisfying assignment for a false statement); equivalently the constraint system has no under-constrained signal:  ¬∃ free signal s, assignments w,w' agreeing on xpub and all constraints but differing on a value that should be determined.
formalization.state_machine: Model the circuit as a constraint relation; soundness = the relation is functional from (public input) to (intended output) — any two satisfying assignments agreeing on public inputs agree on all should-be-determined signals.
formalization.type_theoretic: Special soundness (k accepting transcripts with a common prefix ⇒ extract a witness) gives a constructive extractor; in Curry-Howard terms the proof object literally contains the witness extractable by the verifier's challenge structure.
formalization.hyperproperty: The circuit-determinism surrogate is a 2-safety property (two satisfying assignments must agree), verifiable by self-composition + SMT — which is precisely what under-constraint detectors implement.

relationships.note: Soundness (integrity) and zero-knowledge (privacy) are INDEPENDENT; a complete system needs both.
Computational soundness rests on hardness assumptions (and ROM for Fiat-Shamir).

attack_surface.pattern: an output or intermediate signal is not fully constrained; attacker assigns it freely to satisfy a false statement
incident_refs: UNVERIFIED: numerous public circom/Plonkish audit findings of this class
attack_surface.notes: Detect with Picus/Ecne; the single most common ZK bug class.

attack_surface.pattern: a signal expected to be a bit or in a range is unconstrained, enabling overflow/aliasing in field arithmetic
division/inverse computed in witness without constraining the relation, allowing arbitrary value
attack_surface.notes: Constrain a·a⁻¹=1 and the quotient·divisor+remainder relation.

attack_surface.pattern: challenge derived from an incomplete transcript, enabling grinding / soundness break
incident_refs: 'Frozen Heart' weak-Fiat-Shamir class — VERIFY scope before citing
attack_surface.notes: Hash the FULL transcript including all public inputs and prior messages.

invariant_checkpoints: every signal proven determined by public inputs

strategies.notes: Formally checks every signal is uniquely determined; THIS is where production assurance happens.
Proves the extractor exists under stated assumptions.
Search for two distinct witnesses accepted for the same public input (a soundness counterexample).

testability: no two distinct witnesses accepted for one public input
false statement cannot produce an accepting proof

runtime: on-chain verifier with audited verification key
design_patterns: audited, reproducible trusted setup or transparent setup

assumptions.statement: Underlying hardness assumptions and (for NIZK) ROM hold at the chosen security level.

provenance.notes: The integrity dual of BPO:0003. The record deliberately foregrounds under-constraint as the practical failure mode and separates it from the privacy claim.
